title: Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo: The Complete 2026 Guide
metaDescription: 2026 guide to the Tamasopo waterfalls (Siete Cascadas): prices, hours, how to get there from Ciudad Valles, Hacienda los Gomez, and real travel tips.
excerpt: Prices, hours, the difference between the municipal park and Hacienda los Gomez, and how to get to the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo from Ciudad Valles.
contentHtml:
The Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo (Seven Waterfalls of Tamasopo) are a system of stepped falls in the municipality of Tamasopo, San Luis Potosí, known as one of the most complete water circuits in the Huasteca Potosina. Tamasopo sits in the foothills of the Sierra Madre Oriental, a region where subtropical vegetation meets crystal-clear rivers that have carved canyons and pools over the centuries, creating a landscape that rivals any water destination in Mexico. The municipality of Tamasopo has a human scale that contrasts with the size of its natural landscapes and makes every visit feel far removed from mass tourism. Many travelers arrive with specific questions: Is the main park different from Hacienda Gómez? How much does admission really cost? Can you do it in a day from Ciudad Valles? These questions deserve direct answers, not generalities. The Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo welcome visitors 365 days a year, but the difference between a well-spent visit and an afternoon lost in line comes down to logistical details that rarely appear together in one place.

This guide answers, point by point, every question about how to get to the Tamasopo waterfalls, updated costs, activities, and the difference between the two main entrances to the area. In 2026, admission to the main park costs $60 MXN per person, while Hacienda Gómez—where the seven falls are concentrated—is paid separately, and there the jumps are done with a guide and gear; knowing this before you leave saves you surprises at the ticket booth.

At www.huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators in the region. This guide is updated with real experiences from people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. Last updated: September 2026. Before you read on, book your guided tour in the Huasteca Potosina to make the most of every hour on the road.

What to See and Do at the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo: The Complete Circuit

The Municipal Park: Main Falls and Natural Pools

Tamasopo's municipal park has the widest falls in the system, with blue-green pools where you can swim freely. Admission costs $60 MXN per person in 2026, and parking is paid separately. The park is open every day from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Inside the park there are food stands serving regional dishes—enchiladas potosinas (the state's signature enchiladas, made with chile-tinted dough), agua de tamarindo (a sweet tamarind drink), and seasonal fruit—where a full meal runs about $120–$180 MXN per person, so you don't need to pack lunch if you plan to stay all day. The food stands are usually open from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., although in low season some close earlier, so it's a good idea to bring a snack just in case.

The visitors we coordinate in high season—mainly July and August—confirm that arriving before 10:00 a.m. gets you the best spots at the pools and helps you avoid lines at the entrance. The full inner circuit takes about 3 hours at a relaxed pace, including stops to swim. If you want to combine this park with Puente de Dios on the same day, book the Water Route to Puente de Dios and the Siete Cascadas with transportation included from Ciudad Valles.

Hacienda los Gomez: The Seven Private Falls

Hacienda los Gomez is a private property next to the municipal park where you'll find the stepped waterfalls that give the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo their name. Jumping from pool to pool is always done with a life jacket, helmet, and guide, and you ask about the rate at the entrance; during Holy Week, Christmas, and long holiday weekends, rates can change without notice, so it's smart to bring extra cash.

The route inside Hacienda los Gomez feels more intimate than the main park: dirt trails through dense vegetation, rustic bridges over the river, and smaller but very photogenic falls. For more background on the area's natural setting, check out the guide to Puente de Dios in Tamasopo, which covers the municipality's entire river corridor.

Activities, Prices, and Experiences at the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo in 2026

Real Experience: What First-Time Visitors Can Expect

First-time visitors to the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo tend to underestimate how strong the sun is, combined with the wet trails. The groups we accompany every season describe the first stretch—from the parking lot to the first waterfall—as a steep descent of about 15 minutes on foot, with stone steps; it isn't suitable for wheelchairs or strollers. The water stays at an average of 22-24 °C year-round, which makes it perfect for swimming even in the dry season, from January to March.

In the rainy season (June to October), the water flow increases considerably and the pools get deeper, but the current in some areas can be stronger than usual. Always respect the danger-zone signs inside the park. Going with a local guide significantly reduces that risk: see available tours in the Huasteca Potosina.

How Much Does It Cost to Visit the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo in 2026?

Here's the full cost breakdown for 2026: admission to the municipal park is $60 MXN per person, plus parking; at Hacienda los Gomez the visit includes a guide and gear, and you ask about the rate there. If you choose an organized tour that includes the Puente de Dios Water Route plus the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo, the price is $1,600 MXN per person, with free cancellation up to 48 hours in advance.

On the Tamasopo–Puente de Dios corridor, July is the period with the highest demand and the longest waits at the ticket booth. Tips Before Visiting the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo

Preparing well makes the difference between a smooth day and one full of setbacks. These tips come from the experience we've built up accompanying hundreds of groups every year in the Huasteca Potosina, from families with small children to couples and groups of friends in high season.

  • Arrive before 10:00 a.m.: The park opens at 8:00 a.m., and the first people in get the best spots at the pools; by midday the parking lots fill up and the wait can top 30 minutes.
  • Wear water shoes: The inner trails have slippery stretches over wet rock; water sandals or neoprene water socks protect your feet better than beach flip-flops. Check the packing checklist for the jungle of San Luis Potosí so you don't forget anything essential.
  • Bring biodegradable sunscreen: Regular sunscreen is banned in the pools to protect the ecosystem, and the parks check for it at some entrances. In the guide to the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina, you'll find more details on conditions month by month.
  • A waterproof bag for electronics: The spray from the smaller falls at Hacienda los Gomez easily soaks cameras and phones; a dry bag that costs less than $50 MXN is the best investment of the trip.
  • Bring enough cash: The ticket booths at both entrances don't always have a working card terminal. Plan on at least $500 MXN per person in cash to cover admission, parking, food at the local stands, and maybe a handicraft or two at the entrance.

How Do You Get to the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo from Ciudad Valles?

Tamasopo is 49 km from Ciudad Valles on federal highway 70, heading toward the state capital, San Luis Potosí. In normal traffic, the drive takes 45 to 55 minutes. If you're going on your own, it's best to leave Ciudad Valles between 7:30 and 8:00 a.m. to reach the park in its first hour and enjoy the pools before they get crowded. Most visitors arrive in their own vehicle, while the rest use public transportation or organized tours from the city.

By Car or Bus: Step by Step

From Ciudad Valles, take highway 70 west toward Rioverde. At 49 km you'll see signs for Tamasopo; the turnoff to the park is well marked from the main junction. If you're traveling by bus, the lines that run the Ciudad Valles–San Luis Potosí route stop in Tamasopo; a ticket costs about $90–120 MXN in 2026, and the trip takes around 1 hour with stops. From the town of Tamasopo to the park it's 2 km, which you can cover by mototaxi (a motorized three-wheeler) for $30–40 MXN.

Transportation Options and Organized Tours

If you'd rather not drive, organized tours from Ciudad Valles combine the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo with Puente de Dios on the same day, with coordinated pickup and return. This option is especially recommended in the rainy season, when water can pool on some stretches of the secondary road. Frequently Asked Questions About the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo

What's the difference between the Tamasopo park and Hacienda los Gomez?

The municipal park is the main entrance, with the biggest falls and the widest pools; admission costs $60 MXN in 2026. Hacienda los Gomez is a private property next door where you'll find the seven most photogenic stepped falls; it has its own entrance, the jumps are done with a life jacket, helmet, and guide, and you ask about the rate there. Many travelers visit both on the same day.

How much does it cost in total to visit the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo, including parking?

The municipal park charges $60 MXN per person, and parking is paid separately at each entrance. At Hacienda los Gomez, the jumps include a guide and gear, and you ask about the rate there. If you'd rather not add it all up, the Water Route costs $1,600 MXN per person, with Puente de Dios, transportation, admission, and guide included.

How do you get to the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo from Ciudad Valles by bus?

Take any bus on the Ciudad Valles–San Luis Potosí route along highway 70 and ask the driver to let you off in Tamasopo. The ride takes about 1 hour, and a ticket costs between $90 and $120 MXN in 2026. From the center of town, a mototaxi gets you to the park in 5 minutes for $30–40 MXN.

Are the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo safe for families with small children?

Yes, with some specific precautions. The pools in the municipal park have shallow areas suitable for children; however, the trails have wet stone steps that require proper footwear. For families planning things to do in Tamasopo with kids, it's best to avoid the peak of the rainy season (September–October), when the current is strongest. Bringing life jackets for children is recommended, though not required.

Can you visit the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo and Puente de Dios on the same day?

Yes, it's one of the most common itineraries in the area. The two sites are about 8 km apart by car, a drive of about 10–15 minutes on a local road. The ideal plan is to arrive at the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo when they open (8:00 a.m.), spend about 3 hours there, and then move on to Puente de Dios around midday, taking advantage of the light that filters into the canyon between 11:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m. Organized tours from Ciudad Valles handle this circuit as a full-day trip with coordinated transportation; you can check availability and prices here.

Is there a bag check or lockers at the Tamasopo park?

The municipal park doesn't have formal lockers, but at the entrance there are handicraft stalls and shops where some vendors will hold bags or backpacks for a voluntary tip of $20–30 MXN. The most practical thing is to bring only the essentials for the day: a small waterproof bag with your phone, cash, and sunscreen. If you're on an organized tour, the guide usually keeps an eye on valuables while you're in the pools.
